title: Contrastive learning
reading: The slide frames supervised classification as an instance of contrastive learning: the objective maximizes similarity for positive pairs and minimizes it for negative pairs. A diagram on the right illustrates this with image embeddings as queries and class-label embeddings as keys, forming a query-key similarity matrix.

visuals.description: Five images (polar bear, shark, chess pieces, dog, flower) pass through a green trapezoid 'image encoder' producing a column of queries q0...qN. Above, a vocabulary row (chess, bear, dog, ..., flower, ..., shark) maps to a purple row of keys k0...kK. A grid of dot products q_i k_j is shown, with the correct (positive) pairs highlighted in blue: q0k1, q1kK, q2k0, ..., qNk9.
visuals.assertion: Classification is a similarity matrix between image queries and class-name keys, where the labeled ground-truth cells are the positive pairs to maximize and all other cells are negatives to minimize.

concepts.name: Contrastive learning
